en svømmehal.explanation: "En svømmehal" means "an indoor swimming pool". It is built from "at svømme" (to swim) and "en hal" (a hall).

en svømmetur.explanation: "En svømmetur" means "a swim". It is built from "at svømme" (to swim) and "en tur" (a trip).

en sweater.explanation: "En sweater" means "a sweater". To say you are wearing one, use "at have ... på" (literally "to have ... on"): "Jeg har en sweater på" (I am wearing a sweater).

en sygdom.explanation: "En sygdom" means "a disease". It is built from "syg" (sick). To say a person is sick, use "syg" instead: "Hun er syg" (She is sick).

en sygemelding.explanation: "En sygemelding" means "a sick note / sick leave". To say you call in sick, use "at melde sig syg" (literally "to report oneself sick"): "Jeg melder mig syg i dag" (I am calling in sick today).

en sygeplejerske.explanation: "En sygeplejerske" means "a nurse". It is built from "sygepleje" (nursing). To talk about a male nurse, use the same word: "Min bror er sygeplejerske" (My brother is a nurse).

en synagoge.explanation: "En synagoge" means "a synagogue". English speakers should note the Danish spelling ends in "-goge", not "-gogue". A well-known synagogue in Denmark is in "Krystalgade" in Copenhagen.

en synd.explanation: "En synd" means "a sin". To say you feel sorry for someone, use "synd" with no religious meaning: "Det er synd for ham" (I feel sorry for him). To say something is a pity, use it the same way: "Det er synd, at det regner" (It is a pity that it rains).

en synder.explanation: "En synder" means "a sinner". To ask who is to blame for something small, use it for the culprit: "Hvem er synderen?" (Who is the culprit?)

en synkronisering.explanation: "En synkronisering" means "a sync". It comes from "at synkronisere" (to synchronize). To say sound and picture are not timed together, use it for the timing: "Synkroniseringen af lyd og billede er dårlig" (The sync of sound and picture is bad).

en synsvinkel.explanation: "En synsvinkel" means "a point of view / angle". It is built from "syn" (sight) and "en vinkel" (an angle). To talk about the real place you look from, use it for a physical angle: "Fra den synsvinkel kan man se hele byen" (From that angle you can see the whole city).

en syre.explanation: "En syre" means "an acid". It is close to "sur" (sour). To say something tastes sour, use "sur": "Æblet er surt" (The apple is sour).

en sæk.explanation: "En sæk" means "a sack". To name what is in the sack, put it after: "en sæk mel" (a sack of flour). To say backpack, add "ryg" (back) in front: "en rygsæk" (a backpack).

en sæl.explanation: "En sæl" means "a seal". To mean the seal on a document, use a different word, "et segl": "Brevet har et rødt segl" (The letter has a red seal).

en sælger.explanation: "En sælger" means "a salesperson". It comes from "at sælge" (to sell). To say what someone does for a living: "Hun er sælger i en bilforretning" (She is a salesperson at a car dealership).

en sælgerske.explanation: "En sælgerske" means "a saleswoman". It is "en sælger" (a salesperson) with the ending "-ske", which makes the word feminine. The same ending is in "en sygeplejerske" (a nurse).

en sæson.explanation: "En sæson" means "a season", as in a TV season or a sports season. To name the time when something is in demand, put the thing before it: "jordbærsæsonen" (the strawberry season). For spring, summer, fall and winter, use "en årstid" (a season of the year): "Min yndlingsårstid er sommer" (My favorite season is summer).

en sæsonbillet.explanation: "En sæsonbillet" means "a season ticket". It is built from "en sæson" (a season) and "en billet" (a ticket). A similar word is "et sæsonkort" (a season pass): "Jeg har købt et sæsonkort" (I have bought a season pass).

en sætning.explanation: "En sætning" means "a sentence", as in grammar. To ask someone to write one: "Skriv en sætning" (Write a sentence). For a prison sentence, use "en dom" (a verdict): "Han fik en dom på to år" (He got a sentence of two years).

en sø.explanation: "En sø" means "a lake". Do not mix it up with "et hav" (a sea): "Skibet sejler på havet" (The ship sails on the sea).

en søgemaskine.explanation: "En søgemaskine" means "a search engine". It is built from "at søge" (to search) and "en maskine" (a machine). To say you search online: "Jeg søger på nettet efter en cykel" (I am searching online for a bike).

en sølvfisk.explanation: "En sølvfisk" means "a silverfish". It is built from "sølv" (silver) and "en fisk" (a fish), but the animal is an insect. To talk about more than one, the word does not change: "to sølvfisk" (two silverfish).

en søn.explanation: "En søn" means "a son". To say son-in-law, add "sviger" (in-law) in front: "en svigersøn" (a son-in-law). To say how old a son is: "Min søn er fem år" (My son is five years old).

en søndagsmiddag.explanation: "En søndagsmiddag" means "a Sunday dinner". It is built from "en søndag" (a Sunday) and "en middag" (a dinner). The word "middag" is also in other dinners, such as "en julemiddag" (a Christmas dinner).

en søster.explanation: "En søster" means "a sister". To say a sister shares only one parent, use "en halvsøster" (a half sister): "Min halvsøster bor i Aarhus" (My half sister lives in Aarhus). The plural is "søstre", not "søstere": "Jeg har to søstre" (I have two sisters).

en søstjerne.explanation: "En søstjerne" means "a starfish". It is built from "sø" (sea) and "en stjerne" (a star). The same "sø" means sea in "en søløve" (a sea lion).

et s-tog.explanation: "Et S-tog" means "an S-train". It is the commuter train network around Copenhagen. The part "tog" (train) is also in "et godstog" (a freight train).

et salg.explanation: "Et salg" means "a sale". To say something is offered for sale, use "til salg": "Huset er til salg" (The house is for sale). For a sale with lower prices, use "et udsalg" (a clearance sale): "Der er udsalg i dag" (There is a sale today).

et samarbejde.explanation: "Et samarbejde" means "a collaboration". It is built from "sam" (together) and "et arbejde" (work). To name who you work with, use "i samarbejde med" (in cooperation with): "Vi laver det i samarbejde med kommunen" (We are doing it in cooperation with the municipality).

et samfund.explanation: "Et samfund" means "a society". To talk about people in general, use "i samfundet" (in society): "Alle i samfundet skal betale skat" (Everyone in society has to pay tax). The word is also in "samfundsfag" (social studies), a school subject in Denmark: "Vi har samfundsfag i dag" (We have social studies today).

et samfundsproblem.explanation: "Et samfundsproblem" means "a social problem". It is built from "et samfund" (a society) and "et problem" (a problem). The part "samfunds-" is also in "samfundsfag" (social studies), a school subject in Denmark: "Vi har samfundsfag i dag" (We have social studies today).

et samliv.explanation: "Et samliv" means "a life together". It is built from "sam" (together) and "et liv" (a life). To say how long a couple has been together: "Deres samliv har varet i ti år" (Their life together has lasted ten years).

et sammenskudsgilde.explanation: "Et sammenskudsgilde" means "a potluck". It is built from "at skyde sammen" (to chip in together) and "et gilde" (a feast). The same "at skyde sammen" is used when people share a cost: "Vi skyder sammen til en gave" (We are chipping in for a gift).

et sammenstød.explanation: "Et sammenstød" means "a clash / collision". It is built from "sammen" (together) and "et stød" (a bump). To say two cars hit each other: "Der var et sammenstød mellem to biler" (There was a collision between two cars). To say two people disagree sharply: "Der var et hårdt sammenstød mellem de to politikere" (There was a harsh clash between the two politicians).

et sammentræf.explanation: "Et sammentræf" means "a coincidence". To react to a surprising coincidence, say: "Sikke et sammentræf!" (What a coincidence!) The same "sikke et ..." works for other surprises: "Sikke et vejr!" (What weather!)

et samtaleemne.explanation: "Et samtaleemne" means "a topic of conversation". It is built from "en samtale" (a conversation) and "et emne" (a topic). To ask someone to talk about something else: "Kan vi skifte samtaleemne?" (Can we change the subject?)

et samvær.explanation: "Et samvær" means "a time together". To say you enjoyed the company, use the form "godt samvær" (good company): "Vi nød det gode samvær" (We enjoyed the good company). In family matters, it also means the time a child spends with the parent they do not live with: "Hvornår har faren samvær med børnene?" (When does the father have time with the children?)

et sankthansbål.explanation: "Et sankthansbål" means "a Midsummer bonfire". It is built from "Sankt Hans" (Saint John) and "et bål" (a bonfire). In Denmark, it is lit on the evening of 23 June. A straw witch, "en heks" (a witch), is burned on the fire.

et sejl.explanation: "Et sejl" means "a sail". The verb "at sejle" (to sail) comes from the same stem. It means to travel by any boat, even one without a sail: "Færgen sejler til Sverige" (The ferry sails to Sweden).

et sekund.explanation: "Et sekund" means "a second", as on a clock. To ask someone to wait a short moment, use "et øjeblik" (a moment) instead: "Et øjeblik, tak" (One moment, please).

et selskab.explanation: "Et selskab" means "a company / gathering". To talk about a party, use it for a gathering of people: "Vi var til et selskab hos naboerne" (We were at a party at the neighbors'). To talk about a business, it is the end of words like "et forsikringsselskab" (an insurance company): "Han arbejder i et forsikringsselskab" (He works at an insurance company).

et semester.explanation: "Et semester" means "a semester". To name which semester, put the season before it: "efterårssemestret" (the autumn semester) and "forårssemestret" (the spring semester).

et senat.explanation: "Et senat" means "a senate". Denmark has no senate, only one house called "Folketinget" (the Danish parliament).

et shot.explanation: "Et shot" means "a shot", as in a small strong drink. To name the drink, put it after "shot": "et shot tequila" (a shot of tequila).

et show.explanation: "Et show" means "a show". To talk about a talk show on television, use "et talkshow" (a talk show): "Han er vært i et talkshow" (He hosts a talk show).

et sidespor.explanation: "Et sidespor" means "a digression / sidetrack". It is built from "en side" (a side) and "et spor" (a track). On a railway, it is also a siding: "Toget holder på et sidespor" (The train is standing on a siding).

et signal.explanation: "Et signal" means "a signal". To say someone sends a signal, use "at give et signal" (to give a signal): "Hun gav et signal med hånden" (She gave a signal with her hand). To say your phone has no reception: "Jeg har ikke noget signal her" (I do not have any signal here).

et sind.explanation: "Et sind" means "a mind". To describe someone who listens to new ideas: "et åbent sind" (an open mind). To say what someone intends, use "at have i sinde" (to intend): "Hvad har du i sinde?" (What do you intend to do?)

et siv.explanation: "Et siv" means "a rush", as in the plant. The plural is the same as the singular: "to siv" (two rushes).

et skab.explanation: "Et skab" means "a cupboard". To name the kind of cupboard, add a word in front: "et køleskab" (a refrigerator, literally "a cooling cupboard").

et skattekort.explanation: "Et skattekort" means "a tax card". It is built from "en skat" (a tax) and "et kort" (a card). In Denmark, the tax card is digital, and your employer gets it from the tax authorities.

et skelet.explanation: "Et skelet" means "a skeleton". To talk about the bare frame of a building, use the same word: "Husets skelet er rejst" (The frame of the house is up).

et skema.explanation: "Et skema" means "a schedule / a form". To ask about today's lessons at school: "Hvad står der på skemaet i dag?" (What is on the schedule today?) To tell someone to fill in a form: "Udfyld skemaet" (Fill in the form).

et skib.explanation: "Et skib" means "a ship". To say you are on a ship: "Vi er ombord på skibet" (We are on board the ship). For a small boat, use "en båd" (a boat): "Vi tog en båd over søen" (We took a boat across the lake).

et skift.explanation: "Et skift" means "a shift / change". To say a change in a plan: "et skift i planen" (a change in the plan). To name a work shift, put the time of day before it: "et natskift" (a night shift).

et skilt.explanation: "Et skilt" means "a sign". To say a road sign: "et vejskilt" (a road sign). The same word "skilt" also means "divorced": "Hun er skilt" (She is divorced).

et skind.explanation: "Et skind" means "a skin / hide". To name the animal, put it before "skind": "et fåreskind" (a sheepskin). For a person's skin, use "en hud" (skin) instead: "Min hud er tør" (My skin is dry).

et skjold.explanation: "Et skjold" means "a shield". To say coat of arms, add "våben" (weapon) in front: "et våbenskjold" (a coat of arms).

et skohorn.explanation: "Et skohorn" means "a shoehorn". It is built from "en sko" (a shoe) and "et horn" (a horn).

et skolefag.explanation: "Et skolefag" means "a school subject". It is built from "en skole" (a school) and "et fag" (a subject). To say your favorite subject, use "yndlingsfag" (favorite subject): "Matematik er mit yndlingsfag" (Math is my favorite subject).

et skoleår.explanation: "Et skoleår" means "a school year". It is built from "en skole" (a school) and "et år" (a year). In Denmark, the school year starts in August.

et skridt.explanation: "Et skridt" means "a step", as in a footstep. To say something is an important move in a plan: "Det er et vigtigt skridt" (It is an important step). For a step on a stairway, use "et trin" (a step): "Pas på det sidste trin" (Watch the last step).

et skrig.explanation: "Et skrig" means "a scream". It comes from the verb "at skrige" (to scream). To say someone lets out a scream: "Hun udstødte et skrig" (She let out a scream).

et skrivebord.explanation: "Et skrivebord" means "a desk". It is built from "at skrive" (to write) and "et bord" (a table). The same "skrive" is in "en skrivemaskine" (a typewriter).

et skud.explanation: "Et skud" means "a shot", as from a gun. To say you heard a gunshot: "Vi hørte et skud" (We heard a shot). For a small strong drink, use "et shot" (a shot): "Vi drak hver et shot" (We each drank a shot).

et skudsår.explanation: "Et skudsår" means "a gunshot wound". It is built from "et skud" (a shot) and "et sår" (a wound). The same "sår" is in "et knivsår" (a stab wound). Do not mix it up with "et skudår" (a leap year): "Næste år er et skudår" (Next year is a leap year).

et skudår.explanation: "Et skudår" means "a leap year". The extra day is "en skuddag" (a leap day): "Den 29. februar er en skuddag" (29 February is a leap day). Do not mix it up with "et skudsår" (a gunshot wound): "Han har et skudsår i benet" (He has a gunshot wound in his leg).

et skuespil.explanation: "Et skuespil" means "a play", as in theater. To say you go to see one: "Vi skal se et skuespil i aften" (We are going to see a play tonight). Do not mix it up with "en skuespiller" (an actor): "Skuespilleren glemte sin replik" (The actor forgot his line).

et skur.explanation: "Et skur" means "a shed". To say where things are kept: "Cyklerne står i skuret" (The bikes are in the shed). The word is also the end of "et regnskur" (a rain shower).

et skybrud.explanation: "Et skybrud" means "a cloudburst". It is built from "en sky" (a cloud) and "et brud" (a break), so it is literally "a cloud break". In Copenhagen, a big cloudburst on 2 July 2011 flooded many streets.

et skydevåben.explanation: "Et skydevåben" means "a firearm". It is built from "at skyde" (to shoot) and "et våben" (a weapon).

et skæg.explanation: "Et skæg" means "a beard". For a mustache, use "et overskæg" (literally "an over-beard"): "Han har et overskæg" (He has a mustache).

et skænderi.explanation: "Et skænderi" means "an argument". It comes from the verb "at skændes" (to quarrel). To say two people had an argument: "De havde et skænderi om penge" (They had an argument about money).

et skærebræt.explanation: "Et skærebræt" means "a cutting board". It is built from "at skære" (to cut) and "et bræt" (a board). The same "bræt" is in "et strygebræt" (an ironing board).

et skærmbillede.explanation: "Et skærmbillede" means "a screenshot". It is built from "en skærm" (a screen) and "et billede" (a picture). To ask someone to send one: "Kan du sende et skærmbillede?" (Can you send a screenshot?)

et skøn.explanation: "Et skøn" means "an estimate / judgment". To give your own estimate, use "efter mit skøn" (by my estimate): "Efter mit skøn tager det en time" (By my estimate it takes an hour). Do not mix it up with the adjective "skøn" (lovely): "Det er en skøn dag" (It is a lovely day).

et slag.explanation: "Et slag" means "a blow / battle". To say someone was hit: "Han fik et slag i ansigtet" (He got a blow to the face). To name a battle: "Slaget ved Dybbøl" (the Battle of Dybbøl). The same word is in "et hjerteslag" (a heartbeat).

et slagord.explanation: "Et slagord" means "a slogan". It is built from "et slag" (a blow) and "et ord" (a word). To ask someone what their slogan is: "Hvad er jeres slagord?" (What is your slogan?)

et slagsmål.explanation: "Et slagsmål" means "a fight", with fists and blows. For a fight with words, use "et skænderi" (an argument): "De havde et skænderi" (They had an argument).

et slagtilfælde.explanation: "Et slagtilfælde" means "a stroke". It is built from "et slag" (a blow) and "et tilfælde" (a case). To say someone had a stroke: "Han fik et slagtilfælde" (He had a stroke).

et slips.explanation: "Et slips" means "a tie". To say you put on a tie: "Han tager slips på" (He puts on a tie).

et slot.explanation: "Et slot" means "a castle". To say a palace, use the same word: "Amalienborg Slot" (Amalienborg Palace).

et smagsløg.explanation: "Et smagsløg" means "a taste bud". It is built from "smag" (taste) and "et løg" (an onion), so it is literally "a taste onion". To say a dish is exciting to taste: "pirre smagsløgene" (to excite the taste buds).

et smil.explanation: "Et smil" means "a smile". The matching verb is "at smile" (to smile): "Hun smiler" (She is smiling). To say how someone answers: "Hun svarede med et smil" (She answered with a smile).

et smykke.explanation: "Et smykke" means "a piece of jewelry". To talk about jewelry in general, use the plural "smykker": "Hun elsker smykker" (She loves jewelry).

et småbarn.explanation: "Et småbarn" means "a toddler". It is built from "små" (small) and "et barn" (a child). The plural is "småbørn", not "småbarn": "Der er mange småbørn på legepladsen" (There are many toddlers on the playground).

et smørrebrød.explanation: "Et smørrebrød" means "an open sandwich". It is built from "smør" (butter) and "et brød" (bread). In Denmark, it is a traditional dish made on "rugbrød" (rye bread). The plural is the same as the singular: "to smørrebrød" (two open sandwiches).

et snefnug.explanation: "Et snefnug" means "a snowflake". It is built from "sne" (snow) and "et fnug" (a bit of fluff). To say big snowflakes are falling: "Der falder store snefnug" (Big snowflakes are falling).

et snit.explanation: "Et snit" means "a cut / average". To say a cut in cloth: "et snit i stoffet" (a cut in the fabric). To say an average, you can also use "et gennemsnit" (an average): "Hendes gennemsnit er 9,5" (Her average is 9.5).

et snørebånd.explanation: "Et snørebånd" means "a shoelace". It is built from "at snøre" (to lace up) and "et bånd" (a band). The same "bånd" is in "et armbånd" (a bracelet).

et sofabord.explanation: "Et sofabord" means "a coffee table". It is built from "en sofa" (a sofa) and "et bord" (a table). The same "bord" is in "et spisebord" (a dining table): "Vi spiser ved spisebordet" (We eat at the dining table).

et solbær.explanation: "Et solbær" means "a blackcurrant". It is built from "en sol" (a sun) and "et bær" (a berry). Do not mix it up with "et ribs" (a redcurrant): "Solbær er sorte, og ribs er røde" (Blackcurrants are black, and redcurrants are red).

et solcenter.explanation: "Et solcenter" means "a tanning salon". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "et center" (a center). The same "sol" is in "en solbrille" (sunglasses): "Jeg har glemt mine solbriller" (I have forgotten my sunglasses).

et solhverv.explanation: "Et solhverv" means "a solstice". To name which solstice, put the season in front: "sommersolhverv" (the summer solstice) and "vintersolhverv" (the winter solstice).

et solpanel.explanation: "Et solpanel" means "a solar panel". It is built from "en sol" (a sun) and "et panel" (a panel).

et solstik.explanation: "Et solstik" means "a sunstroke". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "et stik" (a sting), so it is literally "a sun sting". The same "stik" is in "et myggestik" (a mosquito bite).

et sommerhus.explanation: "Et sommerhus" means "a summer house". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "et hus" (a house). To say you rent one: "Vi lejer et sommerhus i Jylland" (We are renting a summer house in Jutland).

et sommerhusområde.explanation: "Et sommerhusområde" means "a summer house area". It is built from "et sommerhus" (a summer house) and "et område" (an area).

et sommerjob.explanation: "Et sommerjob" means "a summer job". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "et job" (a job). To ask if someone has work this summer: "Har du et sommerjob?" (Do you have a summer job?)

et sortiment.explanation: "Et sortiment" means "an assortment". To say a shop sells many kinds of goods: "Butikken har et bredt sortiment" (The shop has a wide range).
